title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — Premium Revision Paper #20

pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sound is whispered, with no buzz in the throat? (1 mark)
   A. /g/
   B. /f/
   C. /d/
   D. /v/

2. What should you do before using a website for facts? (1 mark)
   A. Believe everything
   B. Ask a teacher or parent and check the fact elsewhere
   C. Copy it without reading
   D. Share your address

3. Which article goes before 'hour'? (1 mark)
   A. a
   B. the
   C. an
   D. no article always

4. What is the plural of 'box'? (1 mark)
   A. boxes
   B. boxen
   C. boxs
   D. boxies

5. A factual question has an answer that (1 mark)
   A. is not in the text
   B. you invent
   C. is a joke
   D. is stated in the text

6. Which sentence uses 'a lot of' correctly? (1 mark)
   A. There are lot of children in the yard.
   B. There are a lot children in the yard.
   C. There are alot of children in the yard.
   D. There are a lot of children in the yard.

7. 'She reads a lot.' Here 'a lot' means (1 mark)
   A. often or much
   B. never
   C. a place
   D. only one book

8. A red octagon sign with the word STOP tells drivers to (1 mark)
   A. stop completely
   B. turn on lights
   C. park
   D. go faster

9. Which is a possessive pronoun? (1 mark)
   A. your
   B. you
   C. yours
   D. yourself

10. Which is a good rule for writing an SMS? (1 mark)
   A. Use secret code
   B. Leave out your name
   C. Be polite, short and clear
   D. Send it to strangers

11. Independent reading means (1 mark)
   A. reading only for exams
   B. reading aloud to the class only
   C. copying sentences
   D. reading on your own without being told what to read

12. What is the superlative of 'good'? (1 mark)
   A. most good
   B. goodest
   C. best
   D. better

13. Which detail uses the sense of smell? (1 mark)
   A. I heard a bell.
   B. I saw a table.
   C. I could smell fresh bread.
   D. I touched a wall.

14. At the end of a yes or no question, the voice usually (1 mark)
   A. stays low always
   B. rises
   C. falls
   D. stops

15. A high, rising voice when we say 'Really?' shows (1 mark)
   A. sleep
   B. surprise
   C. boredom
   D. anger only

16. Quantifiers: Choose the correct sentence. (1 mark)
   A. How much water do you drink?
   B. How much waters do you drink?
   C. How many waters do you drink?
   D. How many water do you drink?

17. A pictorial composition is (1 mark)
   A. a map
   B. a song
   C. a shopping list
   D. a story written from a set of pictures

18. Pictures and stories: Which sentence describes a feeling? (1 mark)
   A. The computer was on.
   B. The message travelled.
   C. He clicked Send.
   D. She was very happy to hear from him.

19. What does the proverb 'A friend in need is a friend indeed' mean? (1 mark)
   A. A friend must be rich
   B. A true friend helps you when you are in trouble
   C. Friends are only for games
   D. Friends should never ask for help

20. Choose the correct -ing form of 'lie' (to rest flat). (1 mark)
   A. liing
   B. lying
   C. lieing
   D. lyeing

21. How is the sound /v/ made? (1 mark)
   A. The lips are rounded and do not touch the teeth
   B. The upper teeth touch the lower lip and the voice buzzes
   C. The tongue touches the roof and there is no voice
   D. The mouth is closed and air passes through the nose

22. What is an inference? (1 mark)
   A. A spelling mistake
   B. The title of a passage
   C. A word from the text copied exactly
   D. Something not stated directly that you work out from clues

23. What is reader's theatre? (1 mark)
   A. Silent reading
   B. Copying a script
   C. Acting a play with full costumes
   D. Reading parts from a script with only your voice, without costumes or sets

24. What is the short form of 'let us'? (1 mark)
   A. le'ts
   B. let's
   C. let'us
   D. lets'

25. Which sentence would best begin a narrative about a farm visit? (1 mark)
   A. Last Saturday, my class visited a farm near our school.
   B. I like cows.
   C. The farm is nice.
   D. Farms grow food.

26. Which pair of words differs only in /h/ and /f/? (1 mark)
   A. cat and cap
   B. sit and seat
   C. hill and fill
   D. ship and sheep

27. Which end mark is right for: 'How many books have you read'? (1 mark)
   A. ?
   B. .
   C. ,
   D. !

28. What is the answer to this riddle? 'I am used to wash the body. I make bubbles and get smaller each time you use me.' (1 mark)
   A. a bucket
   B. a towel
   C. soap
   D. a broom

29. Which word has the long vowel /iː/? (1 mark)
   A. ship
   B. sit
   C. bit
   D. sheep

30. What is a factual text? (1 mark)
   A. A joke
   B. A made-up story only
   C. A text that gives true information
   D. A poem only

31. Why should water from rivers be boiled before drinking? (1 mark)
   A. It tastes sweet
   B. It is too cold
   C. It may contain germs
   D. It is too clear

32. Which conjunction joins two negative ideas? (1 mark)
   A. nor
   B. or
   C. and
   D. so

33. What does 'for' mean when it is used as a conjunction? (1 mark)
   A. however
   B. before
   C. although
   D. because

34. Which word means 'the leader of a team'? (1 mark)
   A. captain
   B. kit
   C. whistle
   D. stadium

35. 'Who's' is a short form of which words? (1 mark)
   A. who has not
   B. whose is
   C. who is
   D. who was not

36. After 'does' or 'did', which form of the main verb do we use? (1 mark)
   A. The plural form
   B. The past participle
   C. The base form
   D. The -ing form

37. What is a proverb? (1 mark)
   A. A long story
   B. A page of a dictionary
   C. A short well-known saying that gives advice or a truth
   D. A kind of song

38. How is a diary different from a letter? (1 mark)
   A. A diary always has an address
   B. A diary is always sent by post
   C. A diary is written for yourself and is not sent
   D. A diary has no date

39. Which sentence uses the pattern 'very ... but ...' correctly? (1 mark)
   A. Very shirt is nice, but.
   B. The shirt is but very nice, it is expensive.
   C. The shirt very nice but expensive.
   D. The shirt is very nice, but it is too expensive.

40. What should you do if a website you find online worries you? (1 mark)
   A. Close it and tell a trusted adult
   B. Share it with everyone
   C. Ignore the adult
   D. Give your address

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Name the three parts of fluent reading and explain each briefly. (3 marks)

42. Write two minimal pairs for /t/ and /d/. (2 marks)

43. Write two ways you can show a speaker that you are listening actively. (2 marks)

44. Explain the meaning of 'tax' and 'fine'. (3 marks)

45. Rewrite using the past perfect: 'The bus left. Then I arrived.' (2 marks)

46. List the three main parts of a composition and say what each does. (3 marks)

47. Give two examples of regular plurals and two of irregular plurals. (2 marks)

48. Write the minimal pairs for: ship, seat, sock. (3 marks)

49. Rewrite in the past tense: 'Today we sweep the compound and plant a tree.' (2 marks)

50. Correct these sentences: (a) Who did scored the goal? (b) When you will come? (3 marks)

51. Rewrite with correct capital letters and full stops: 'we visited lake victoria in august' (3 marks)

52. Underline the prepositions: 'The children ran along the road, past the bank and into the market.' (3 marks)

53. Join with a suitable conjunction: 'I was tired. I finished sweeping.' (2 marks)

54. Write the short forms of: did not, she has, we will, let us. (4 marks)

55. Change to the past progressive: 'The children are singing in the hall.' (2 marks)

56. Correct: (a) 'How much books are there?' (b) 'I do not have some money.' (2 marks)

57. Explain the difference between 'I have eaten' and 'I had eaten when he came.' (3 marks)

58. Copy in neat print: 'Please listen carefully.' Circle the silent letter. (2 marks)

59. Write the subject and the object forms of: I, he, we, they. (2 marks)

60. Make a simple plan for a story called 'The Guests Who Came Late'. (4 marks)

61. Name three parts of a newspaper. (3 marks)

62. Complete the sentences: (a) We have enough plates ___ (eat) the meal. (b) There is enough rice ___ (feed) the guests. (2 marks)

63. Give the meaning of clan, ancestor and adopt. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — /f/
   /f/ is a whispered sound. /v/, /d/ and /g/ are voiced.

2. B — Ask a teacher or parent and check the fact elsewhere
   Checking a second source shows whether the fact is correct.

3. C — an
   The h is silent, so hour starts with a vowel sound.

4. A — boxes
   Nouns ending in x add es.

5. D — is stated in the text
   Factual answers can be found in the words of the passage.

6. D — There are a lot of children in the yard.
   A lot of is written as three words and is followed by a noun.

7. A — often or much
   A lot at the end of a sentence tells how much or how often.

8. A — stop completely
   A stop sign means stop.

9. C — yours
   Yours stands alone and shows ownership.

10. C — Be polite, short and clear
   A good SMS is clear and polite.

11. D — reading on your own without being told what to read
   You choose and read for yourself.

12. C — best
   Good, better, best.

13. C — I could smell fresh bread.
   It describes something smelt.

14. B — rises
   Yes or no questions usually end with a rise.

15. B — surprise
   A rising voice can show surprise.

16. A — How much water do you drink?
   Water is uncountable.

17. D — a story written from a set of pictures
   The pictures guide the events.

18. D — She was very happy to hear from him.
   Was very happy tells a feeling.

19. B — A true friend helps you when you are in trouble
   A true friend is seen when we need help.

20. B — lying
   The letters ie change to y before -ing.

21. B — The upper teeth touch the lower lip and the voice buzzes
   /v/ uses teeth and lip; /w/ uses rounded lips only.

22. D — Something not stated directly that you work out from clues
   Inferential questions need you to use clues.

23. D — Reading parts from a script with only your voice, without costumes or sets
   Reader's theatre uses voices only.

24. B — let's
   The apostrophe replaces the u.

25. A — Last Saturday, my class visited a farm near our school.
   It says when, who and where.

26. C — hill and fill
   'Hill' begins with /h/ and 'fill' with /f/.

27. A — ?
   It is a direct question.

28. C — soap
   Soap makes bubbles and wears away.

29. D — sheep
   'Sheep' has a long /iː/; the others have a short /ɪ/.

30. C — A text that gives true information
   Factual texts share facts.

31. C — It may contain germs
   Boiling kills germs.

32. A — nor
   'Nor' follows a negative.

33. D — because
   'For' gives a reason.

34. A — captain
   The captain leads the team.

35. C — who is
   Who's = who is (or who has).

36. C — The base form
   For example: 'When does she practise?'

37. C — A short well-known saying that gives advice or a truth
   Proverbs teach lessons.

38. C — A diary is written for yourself and is not sent
   A letter is sent to another person.

39. D — The shirt is very nice, but it is too expensive.
   It has 'very' + adjective, then 'but' with the difficulty.

40. A — Close it and tell a trusted adult
   Staying safe means asking for help.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Accuracy: reading the words correctly. Speed: reading at a comfortable, not rushed pace. Expression: using the voice to show meaning and feeling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part explained.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: ten, den and tin, din.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look at the speaker and nod; keep still and quiet; say 'I see'.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tax is money paid to the government to help run the country. A fine is money paid as a punishment for breaking a rule or law.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for showing a difference.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: The bus had left before I arrived. (Or: When I arrived, the bus had left.)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 'had left' and 1 for the linking word.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Introduction: tells who, where and when. Body: tells what happened in order. Conclusion: tells how it ended or how the writer felt.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part with its job.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Regular: books, dishes. Irregular: men, feet.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pair.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: ship and sheep (or sip); seat and sheet (or sit); sock and shock.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct partner word.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Today we swept the compound and planted a tree.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for swept and 1 for planted.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) Who scored the goal? (b) When will you come?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correction and 1 for question marks and capitals.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: We visited Lake Victoria in August.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for We, 1 mark for Lake Victoria and August, 1 mark for the full stop.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: along, past, into
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: I was tired, but I finished sweeping.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a suitable conjunction (but or yet) and 1 for the comma.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: didn't, she's, we'll, let's
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: The children were singing in the hall.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for were, 1 mark for keeping singing.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) How many books are there? (b) I do not have any money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'I have eaten' says the eating is finished and it matters now. 'I had eaten when he came' says I finished eating before he came, in the past.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for the time link.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Please listen carefully. (silent t in listen)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for neat copying and 1 mark for identifying t.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: I, me; he, him; we, us; they, them.
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each pair.

60. (4 marks)
   Answer: Beginning: family prepares for a party. Middle: guests do not arrive, food gets cold. Problem: they lost the way. End: they arrive, everyone laughs and eats.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a beginning, 1 for events, 1 for a problem and 1 for an ending.

61. (3 marks)
   Answer: Masthead (name), headline, byline, article, picture, caption, advert, weather report (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

62. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) to eat (b) to feed
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

63. (3 marks)
   Answer: A clan is a large group of families with the same ancestor. An ancestor is a family member who lived long ago. To adopt is to take a child into your family and raise the child as your own.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning.
